evidence.description: CRIT-016 through CRIT-018 narrowly close the stated browser-helper serialization and emitted-renderer defects without changing the closed score model.
REQ-007 requires rounded, clamped measured ratios and REQ-010 requires malformed score models to fail closed; the contract preserves both obligations.

The emitted-script VM test uses numerator 945755921642804 and denominator 9007199253740991, asserts the canonical value 10, and renders the closed FINANCIAL model; malformed-model rejection tests remain present.
The recorded RED result isolates the emitted browser renderer failure as ReferenceError: roundedScoreValue is not defined for that same canonical safe-integer ratio.

renderPanelPage serializes roundedScoreValue before validScoreOrgan and renderScoreCards, while the module imports that helper from panel-score-semantics.js; this is exactly the CRIT-016 dependency order and reuse rule.
roundedScoreValue is the shared BigInt half-up, 0..100-clamped helper exported by the score core, so CRIT-016 does not authorize a divergent browser formula.
The documented presentation shell renders the closed API model and never recomputes score semantics; serializing the existing validation helper preserves that pure-core/presentation-shell boundary.
CRIT-016 explicitly forbids duplicating or altering the integer-safe formula, and the sprint scope excludes unrelated endpoint, database, and payload changes.
CRIT-018 names the focused, full-regression, evaluation, and PostgreSQL commands with binary exit/count expectations, making the release-preservation gate directly evaluable.
Recorded GREEN evidence shows 14 focused score tests and 14 UI tests passing, including the emitted-browser safe-integer regression.
